prompt:
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Diagram showing vector P as a horizontal arrow from origin O to point A, and vector Q as an upward-sloping arrow starting from point A to point B. A third arrow R connects origin O directly to point B.]
Which statement correctly describes the head-to-tail rule for finding the resultant vector R = P + Q?
options: Place the tail of Q at the head of P, and draw R from the tail of P to the head of Q.
Place the tail of Q at the tail of P, and draw R from the head of P to the head of Q.
Place the head of Q at the head of P, and draw R from origin O to the tail of Q.
Place the tail of Q at the head of P, and draw R from the head of Q back to the tail of P.

answer.explanation: In head-to-tail vector addition, the second vector Q is placed with its tail at the head of the first vector P. The resultant vector R is drawn pointing from the initial start (tail of P) to the final destination (head of Q).

distractor_explanations: Correct. Tail of Q at head of P, with resultant R pointing from the tail of P to the head of Q.
Incorrect. This describes tail-to-tail placement without completing the parallelogram.
Incorrect. Head-to-head placement does not represent head-to-tail addition.
Incorrect. Drawing from finish to start produces the negative of the resultant (-R).
hints: Follow the journey in order: start to intermediate point, then intermediate point to end.
The resultant points from the very beginning to the very end.
solution: In head-to-tail addition, vector Q starts at the head of P. The resultant R connects the start (tail of P) to the finish (head of Q). Option 1 is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Review definition of head-to-tail construction.
Step 2: Vector Q is drawn with its tail at the head (tip) of vector P.
Step 3: Resultant R starts at the tail of P and points to the head of Q.
